hypotheses.justification: `[NeZero N]` comes from `variable (N : ℕ) [NeZero N]`. It becomes an argument only because `N` appears in the statement through `modularFunctionFieldBar N`. Nothing in the statement needs it to elaborate. In `Definitions/Def_ModularCurve_ArithmeticGalois.lean`, `modularFunctionFieldBar` is declared under `variable (N : ℕ)` with no `NeZero` instance, so neither it nor `modularFunctionFieldFull`, which its body uses, can depend on `NeZero N`. The other names in the statement are generic over any field `F` with `[Field F] [Algebra (AlgebraicClosure ℚ) F]` and never mention `N`: `Place` (in `Def_AlgebraicCurve_DivisorClassGroup`), `Place.evalAt` (in `Def_AlgebraicCurve_PlaceEvaluation`), `pivotIndex` (in `Def_ModularCurve_JZeroHeightForm`) and `regVal` (in `Def_AlgebraicCurve_ChordalProximity`). The proof just unfolds the definition, `rw [regVal]; simp only [dif_pos hr]`, so the lemma is a definitional unfolding that holds for every `N`, including `N = 0`. Adding `omit [NeZero N] in` keeps the same proof working. The other arguments are needed: `hr` appears in the conclusion (`pivotIndex s o hr`), and `s`, `o`, `t`, `k`, `e` and `u` all appear in the conclusion.
